summary: SQLite printf formats values using a documented format string and returns text.
documentation: SQLite printf formats values using a documented format string and returns text. A decimal integer format can include zero padding and a minimum field width, allowing numeric values to be displayed as consistent short codes.
inputs: items(id INTEGER, serial INTEGER NOT NULL), with serial in 0..99999.
returns: id and code, ordered by id.
caution: Field width is a minimum, not a truncation limit. Formatting does not validate the identifier or change its stored numeric value. This task uses nonnegative integers only.
scenarios: Format a serial number in a local inventory report.
Produce a consistent short numeric label for a print preview.
Align exported integer codes without changing their stored values.
title: Format minimum-width serials
problem: Return id and printf('%04d',serial) AS code from items, ordered by id. Use at least four decimal digits, padding with zeroes on the left; larger values remain complete.
goal: Use printf() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
